test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Electrician) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A 6-pole alternator is running and producing a frequency of 50 Hz. If the frequency is decreased to 20 Hz, how many poles will be required, if the alternator is to be run at the same speed?
solution:
__Concept__

The speed of an alternator is given by:

N_s={120times fover P}

where, NS = Synchronous speed

f = Frequency

P = No. of pole

__Calculation__

Given, P = 6

f = 50 Hz

The synchronous speed is:

N_s={120times 50over 6}

N_s=1000space rpm

For the same speed, if the frequency is decreased to 25 Hz, then the number of poles is given by:

1000={120times 20over P}

 P = 2.4 

Since the number of poles must be an even integer, the closest valid value is 2.
